answer: A useful defense is to make each agent’s influence depend on a scarce, nontransferable resource that accrues over time, such as a stake locked before it can vote on payments. A newcomer cannot instantly split one identity into a thousand and gain a thousand times the influence: every identity needs its own locked stake, and misbehavior can forfeit it. A raven may wander through a gale of newly registered agents, but the attacker still pays capital for each effective identity and risks losing it if those identities coordinate fraudulently.
